text:
alex: Quick check — onboarding a contractor via SAML/SCIM who needs a temporary 'contractor' role scoped to project:team-alpha for 14 days. Questions: 1) Do our logs ever store full SAML assertions or NameID/email in plain text? 2) Best place to enforce TTL (IdP group expiry vs SCIM user attribute vs our cron)? 3) Approval flow — person-ops only or sec approval too? @people-ops

olivia: Short answers: we do NOT persist raw SAML assertions in production logs. Auth logs store a redacted identifier. SCIM sync events include attributes we send (so be mindful), but we redact sensitive fields in long-term audit stores. Prefer configuring expiry on the IdP group + a SCIM attribute as backup. cc @maria

maria: For contractors we require manager + sec sign-off for elevated roles. People-ops owns the onboarding ticket and final approval. Process: create org-ticket with manager, attach justification, set expiry date — we close/auto-deprovision after expiry. Policy link: https://internal.docs/redwood/security/onboarding#temp-access (internal)

ajay: Ops/runtime notes: map SAML entitlement -> SCIM group rather than embedding roles in the user object if you want easier expiry. We run a daily job that looks for groups with meta.expiry and removes memberships. Snippet we use on the sync worker:```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
  "userName": "contractor.jdoe@example.com",
  "externalId": "okta-12345",
  "entitlements": [{"value": "project:team-alpha","type": "ephemeral","expiry": "2026-04-05T15:00:00Z"}],
  "active": true
}
```

sec-bot: Audit: scheduled deprov job created (job-id: 0xabc123) by ajay — next run 2026-04-06T00:00:00Z :white_check_mark:

people-ops: I can approve once the org-ticket is filed. Please include manager, project owner, expected end date, and sec justification. Our template auto-populates an expiry and triggers the deprov job. Ticket example: ORG-1234.

alex: Thanks — I'll open ORG-1234 and add manager + sec. One follow-up: are emails sent in SCIM payloads masked in our logs or do we need to avoid sending full email?

olivia: It's okay to send email in SCIM. Logs in the auth pipeline mask the local-part by default (e.g., j***@example.com) and long-term audit logs keep only hashed identifiers. Short-lived debug logs (if enabled) may contain more — don't enable debug for production syncs.

ajay: Also note: nested groups can complicate deprov. If the contractor is in a nested group under team-alpha, our current cascade behavior is opt-in. Recommend mapping to a flat SCIM group for ephemeral access.

maria: I'll review the org-ticket once filed and confirm sec approval path. If anyone wants me to pre-check the justification text, ping me.

alex: Perfect — filing now. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
